questions.q: What did Bowlby notice about children in orphanages after the war?
a: They failed to thrive despite food and clothing
They recovered quickly from early separation
They preferred toys to adult caregivers
They bonded equally with every adult
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the children were fed and clothed yet still did not thrive without a caregiver.

questions.q: What did Harlow's monkey experiment suggest about attachment?
a: Comfort and contact matter more than food alone
Food is the strongest driver of bonding
Young animals cannot bond with substitutes
Isolation makes young animals independent
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the baby monkeys chose the soft cloth figure over the wire one that fed them.

questions.q: In the Circle of Security, what is the secure base?
a: The point from which the child departs to explore
The place the child returns to for comfort
The moment when the parent sets limits
The stage when the child stops needing care
questions.why: Lesson 2 places the secure base at nine o'clock, where the child leaves on their journey.

questions.q: Which needs does the summary list while a child explores?
a: Being watched, delighted in, joined and helped
Being corrected, tested and redirected often
Being left completely alone for long periods
Being rewarded with treats for independence
questions.why: Lesson 2 names watching, delighting, enjoying activities together and helping out.

questions.q: What does the summary say repairs a rupture in the circle?
a: Acknowledging the unmet need and apologizing
Pretending the mistake never happened
Giving the child a small gift afterward
Waiting for the child to calm down alone
questions.why: Lesson 3 says naming the need you missed and apologizing teaches that repair follows mistakes.
